name: Naayì
catalog_citation: Andualem Adal Tessema. 2020. A Descriptive Syntax of Naayì. PhD dissertation, Department of Linguistics and Philology, Addis Ababa University. PDF from AAU ETD repository (handle 12345678/21418).
catalog_locator: p.32, sect. 2.7.1 'Is Naayì a Tone Language?'; syllable/tone inventory p.33 (sect. 2.7.2)
catalog_quote: Based on the above definitions, Naayì is a tone language. This is because, the tone of Naayì has both lexical and grammatical functions as illustrated in (§ 2.7.3). As for the typology of a stress language versus a tone language Yip, 2002 4, Naayì is not a stress language as far as any tone-bearing unit (or every syllable) can bear any tone (free tone). The lexical items associated with tonal melodies are also chosen from an unrestricted set of words in Naayì. This means that a set of words in the same word class that have the same syllable structure can be divided into different groups just by their tone melodies' patterns. Hence, Naayì is not stress or accent language; rather it is tonal language. Therefore, this point strengthens Aklilu s 1990 443 work in which it is recognized that Naayì is tonal. ... Naayì has three level tonemes high H, mid M and low L . These three tonemes are …

(2) Deciding source: a 2020 AAU PhD dissertation (332 pp) whose phonology chapter explicitly argues Naayì is a tone language and 'not stress or accent language', with H/M/L level tones freely borne by every syllable and both lexical and grammatical tone functions.
